stances.claim: The 'insufficient law' doctrine -- Santiago v. Comelec's 1997 holding that RA 6735 was inadequate to implement PI -- was effectively reversed by Lambino (2006), where the Court, by a more decisive 10-5 vote, declared RA 6735 'sufficient and adequate' to amend the Constitution via people's initiative; advocates still citing Santiago are citing abandoned jurisprudence.
stances.confidence: asserted with personal-history disclosure ('I should know. I was already an associate justice in 1997')

stances.claim: Lambino v. Comelec correctly rejected the 2006 PI attempt -- the petition failed because the signatories were not shown the full text of the proposed amendments and were only asked about a bicameral-vs-unicameral shift, a 'grand deception' and a 'gigantic fraud'; and the bicameral-to-unicameral switch is a revision, not an amendment, which can only be proposed by con-ass or constitutional convention.

RBH 6 (Zubiri-Legarda-Angara) -- adding 'unless otherwise provided by law' to three nationalistic constitutional restrictions (public utilities, basic education, advertising) -- is structurally clever because the limits stay in place ipso facto unless a future Congress legislates the change, neutralizing the self-service charge.

Belmonte's 2014 attempt at a similar proposal failed because PNoy refused to touch the 1987 Constitution -- 'the great legacy of his deceased mother, Cory Aquino' -- providing a fair historical reminder that Charter change is conditioned by presidential disposition.

Public Filipinos consistently suspect Cha-cha attempts as 'cheap, self-serving schemes to perpetuate the sponsors in power'; today's officials must be transparent and limit changes to those that do not benefit them in any manner -- 'old tricks will no longer work,' especially with the young.

notable_anecdotes: Self-disclosure of own 1997 Santiago dissent -- 'I should know. I was already an associate justice in 1997... In fact, I wrote a strong dissent, saying there was no such thing as an insufficient or inadequate law' -- the rare CJ first-person doctrinal-correction-of-his-younger-self moment.
Self-disclosure of own 2006 Lambino concurrence -- 'I wrote a concurring opinion' -- paired with the unusual personal aside that the seven dissenters were led by Puno 'who later succeeded me as CJ.'
The 6-6 MR-vote-after-Santiago somersaulting -- 'some justices somersaulted' -- a quiet CJ idiom for jurists who changed their votes.
The 'grand deception' and 'gigantic fraud' verbatim from the Lambino ponencia -- used as the doctrinal benchmark against which today's PI proposals must measure.
RBH 6 structural cleverness -- three nationalistic limits (60% public utilities, 60% basic education, 70% advertising) preserved unless Congress acts, blessed by Marcos and Romualdez.

Closing flourish -- 'no longer dance with the old Cha-cha rhythm but swing with ABBA, or do the TikTok, or better still, craze with Taylor Swift' -- the Taylor Swift cultural reference giving the column its memorable title and signaling that traditional Cha-cha framing has aged out of credibility with the young.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban surveys the latest Charter-change (Cha-cha) attempts -- a surreptitious people's initiative reportedly led by some representatives, plus a more open constituent-assembly/normal-legislative path led by Senate leaders. He first clarifies that the 'insufficient law' doctrine -- Santiago v. Comelec's 1997 holding (8-5; MR tied 6-6 as 'some justices somersaulted') that RA 6735 was inadequate to implement PI -- is no longer controlling. He personally dissented in 1997 ('I should know. I was already an associate justice'), arguing 'no such thing as an insufficient or inadequate law.' Nine years later, when he was CJ, the Court in Lambino v. Comelec (Oct 25, 2006, 8-7) -- Carpio ponente, Puno leading dissenters -- rejected another PI attempt because the signatories were not shown the full text of the proposed bicameral-to-unicameral shift, a 'grand deception' and 'gigantic fraud,' and because PI can propose only amendments, not revisions (revisions go to con-ass or constitutional convention). On Nov 21, 2006, MR was denied with finality by the same 8-7 vote, BUT the Court -- by a more decisive 10-5 -- clarified that RA 6735 was 'sufficient and adequate' to amend the Constitution via PI, effectively burying Santiago. Today, Senate President Migz Zubiri, Senate President Pro Tempore Loren Legarda, and Senate Finance Chair Sonny Angara have filed Resolution of Both Houses No. 6, proposing three Cha-cha items through normal legislation by adding 'unless otherwise provided by law' to constitutional provisions limiting public utilities (60% Filipino), basic education other than religious-owned (60% Filipino), and advertising agencies (70% Filipino). The nationalistic limits stay in place ipso facto unless Congress legislates change -- neutralizing the self-service charge with reason and logic -- and the proposal has the blessing of both President Marcos and Speaker Romualdez. A similar Belmonte proposal in 2014 failed because PNoy refused to touch what he considered Cory Aquino's great legacy. Filipinos have consistently frowned on Cha-cha as cheap, self-serving schemes to perpetuate the sponsors in power. Today's officials should be more transparent and limit changes to those that do not benefit them in any manner. 'Perhaps, they should no longer dance with the old Cha-cha rhythm but swing with ABBA, or do the TikTok, or better still, craze with Taylor Swift. Perhaps, just perhaps, our people, especially the young, will begin to believe them.'
